title: the water tower Rising
premise: Emrys Nystrom, the meticulous statistician of the Millbrook High water polo team, has spent five years hiding a family gift for reading probability like sheet music — a gift that once destroyed their grandmother's reputation. When grandma's recipe box yields instructions written in a language of odds and tides, Emrys discovers the Nystroms were wardens of the old water tower, which holds the town's luck in its cistern, and that a powerful family has been siphoning that luck for decades to rig everything from harvests to championships. To expose them, Emrys must win the state championship that everyone watches while secretly contesting the real one — a generations-old wager sealed in the tower's ledger — before the season's final whistle, with the help of rival captain Wren Okafor, the girl they were never supposed to fall for. In the end Emrys breaks the ledger by refusing to play the rigged game at all, flooding the town with fair odds, losing the trophy but winning the tower's trust, Wren's hand, and the inheritance on their own terms.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval grew up in a drought-prone farm town where the water tower was the tallest thing for fifty miles, and never stopped wondering what it was watching over. A former math tutor and amateur baker, they write stories about quiet kids who do loud math.

chapters.title: The Box on the Top Shelf
chapters.summary: Emrys Nystrom, POV. Sorting grandma's kitchen after the funeral, Emrys finds a recipe card for something called 'Fair Odds Stew' with instructions no kitchen could follow. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into curiosity — the first crack in five years of careful silence.

chapters.title: Percentages and Pretending
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. At practice, Emrys quietly adjusts the team's shot charts and notices the water in the pool behaving strangely — currents favoring certain players. Beat: the statistician's unease when data stops obeying.

chapters.title: Card Number Twelve
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. The twelfth card isn't a recipe; it's a map of Millbrook with the water tower circled and a line of numbers that match the town's founding date. Beat: dread and thrill entwined.

chapters.title: Wren Okafor, Perfect Record
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. The rival captain from Delmar Prep scouts Millbrook's pool and catches Emrys predicting plays before they happen. Beat: suspicion with an undercurrent of fascination.

chapters.title: What Grandma Never Baked
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. In grandma's attic, Emrys finds a ledger bound in oilcloth listing every 'harvest, flood, and final' in town history — and the Okafor family name as counterparty. Beat: betrayal of the past bleeding into the present.

chapters.title: The Wager Clause
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. The ledger reveals the tower's cistern holds the town's luck, redistributed each season through a wager between the Nystrom and Okafor lines. Beat: inheritance as a trap, not a gift.

chapters.title: Practice Match
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. A scrimmage against Delmar goes wrong when the water literally turns against Millbrook; Wren sees Emrys fight it barehanded. Beat: the moment rivalry becomes complicity.

chapters.title: Two Truths in a Locker Room
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren confronts Emrys, who lies badly, then stops lying. Beat: the relief of being seen, and the terror of what comes with it.

chapters.title: Rules of the Old Game
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Grandma's cards lay out the hidden contest: each season's final match secretly settles the luck-wager, and the Okafor patriarch has rigged the last forty years. Beat: the scale of the corruption lands.

chapters.title: The Rigged Season
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys audits five years of game data and finds statistical fingerprints of tampering — impossible streaks, tides in the pool. Beat: cold fury replacing fear.

chapters.title: Dinner at the Okafors'
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren's grandfather hosts a 'friendly' dinner, probing Emrys about the recipe box; Wren realizes her own family is the villain of the ledger. Beat: loyalty cracking along family fault lines.

chapters.title: First Card, First Spell
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys attempts 'Fair Odds Stew' in the tower's shadow and briefly equalizes the luck in the pool. Beat: power as responsibility, intoxicating and frightening.

chapters.title: The Cost of Careful
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Flashback chapter: five years ago, Emrys's one careless use of the gift got grandma institutionalized by the Okafors' lawyers. Beat: guilt explained; caution understood.

chapters.title: Allies with Bad Handwriting
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren brings her own family documents — her grandmother's half of the ledger — and the two begin decoding together. Beat: partnership forming over shared inheritance of a lie.

chapters.title: Mid-Season Slump
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. The Okafors notice the equalized luck and retaliate; Millbrook loses three straight and the team fractures. Beat: the personal war bleeding into the public game.

chapters.title: Rain on the Rooftop
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Trapped under the tower during a storm, Emrys and Wren share their fears and almost kiss. Beat: love against duty, first spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Tower's Voice
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Inside the tower, Emrys hears the cistern respond — the luck is not a resource but a living trust that chooses its warden. Beat: the inheritance becomes a relationship.

chapters.title: Grandpa's Ledger, Wren's Name
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren discovers her grandfather has pre-signed her into the next forty years of the wager. Beat: horror of being made an instrument.

chapters.title: Throwing the Game
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. To protect Wren, Emrys considers deliberately losing the hidden wager and letting the Okafors keep the luck. Beat: self-erasure as love, and its rejection.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Grandfather Okafor offers Emrys a place in the system — comfort, safety, Wren — in exchange for silence. Beat: power's corruption made polite and reasonable.

chapters.title: Refusal in Writing
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys declines in a letter read aloud at a town meeting, planting the first public seed of doubt about Millbrook's 'lucky' families. Beat: courage as arithmetic — the odds finally worth taking.

chapters.title: Backlash
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. The Okafors smear Emrys's family; grandma's old institutionalization is weaponized; Wren is benched. Beat: the cost of the refusal, borne together.

chapters.title: The Recipe for Rain
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. A drought card in the box, used in desperation, brings rain but floods the low fields — the gift's power without its ethics. Beat: Emrys becomes what they feared.

chapters.title: Amends in the Cistern
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys climbs the tower and returns the borrowed luck, and the cistern 'forgives' — showing a memory of grandma as a young warden. Beat: reconciliation with the inheritance.

chapters.title: Wren's Defection
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren formally breaks from her grandfather, forfeiting her inheritance, and asks Millbrook to let her play out the season as an enemy of her own name. Beat: duty reversed.

chapters.title: The Team Decides
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys tells the team the truth; some quit, but the core stays, playing now for something real. Beat: found family choosing the fight.

chapters.title: Delmar's Perfect Machine
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Delmar, fully luck-fed, is unbeatable; the Okafors announce the 'final wager' will be settled at states. Beat: the two championships — public and hidden — converge.

chapters.title: Studying the Impossible
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys finds the one statistical anomaly in Delmar's perfection: the luck must be drawn fresh from the tower on game day. Beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Second Thoughts
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren can cut Delmar's supply line but it means destroying her family's last legacy; she hesitates, then refuses to become her grandfather. Beat: integrity over vengeance.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys and Wren on the tower catwalk, trading fears and a first real kiss, agreeing to win honestly or lose honestly. Beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Semifinal: Playing Straight
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Millbrook wins a brutal semifinal with no luck at all — pure skill, pure team. Beat: proof the honest game is worth playing.

chapters.title: The Hidden Bracket
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. The Okafors convene the old wager's court; Wren, as a signatory by blood, demands the final be played under the original fair rules. Beat: using the enemy's law against them.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Gambit
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Okafor accepts — but rigs the tower itself, locking the cistern to his line unless Emrys can reach the valve during the final. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: Championship, First Half
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Down five at half, the tower's stolen luck making Delmar superhuman. Beat: despair, and the team refusing to fold.

chapters.title: Championship, Second Half
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Millbrook claws back on discipline and Wren's insider knowledge; Emrys slips away at the two-minute mark. Beat: the two games running at once.

chapters.title: The Climb
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys climbs the tower during the final minute, the cistern fighting, the ledger burning in their pocket. Beat: climax — body, gift, and will against the inheritance.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Millbrook loses by one as the buzzer sounds — and simultaneously Emrys opens the valve, flooding the town with fair odds. Beat: the championship that didn't matter, lost; the one that did, won.

chapters.title: After the Whistle
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. The town feels the change — small luck, evenly spread; the Okafors' empire of advantage quietly starves; Okafor concedes the ledger. Beat: victory that looks like defeat from the scoreboard.

chapters.title: New Wardens, Old Tower
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Emrys and Wren co-sign a rewritten ledger — stewardship without ownership — as the tower's cistern settles, content. Beat: inheritance transformed into trust.

chapters.title: The Empty Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys writes the final card — 'Recipe for a Fair Season' — and files it in grandma's box for whoever comes next. Beat: peace, love, and the game finally played straight.
